title: Study finds silicon in unirradiated TRISO particles
summary: Researchers at the University of Western Ontario in Canada analyzed TRISO particles and found small regions of silicon in the unirradiated fuel, raising questions about its impact on fuel performance. TRISO particles consist of a central fuel kernel surrounded by layers of carbon and silicon carbide. Silicon is not generally one of the intended elements in the kernel.

title: US Agency Signs Agreement With Oil Company On Study Into SMRs For Turkey
summary: The US Trade and Development Agency (USTDA) has signed an agreement with Turkish oil refiner Tüpraş to fund a study into the potential use of small modular reactors (SMRs) to supply electricity, heat and steam for refinery operations. According to the USTDA, the proposed study will evaluate several US reactor technologies, including their technical and economic feasibility, environmental performance, regulatory requirements and potential industrial applications. The agreement is also expected to develop a roadmap to support Tüpraş in deciding whether to proceed with SMR deployment.

title: Power safely restored to Entergy Mississippi customers
summary: Entergy Mississippi has restored power to the customers in Lawrence County near Monticello, due to the wildfire in the area. Approximately 179 customers were originally taken offline as a proactive safety measure to help protect the public from wildfire hazards. Source

title: Deep Isolation Announces Start Of Site Preparation At Texas Demonstration Project
summary: US-based nuclear waste disposal technology company Deep Isolation Nuclear has begun site preparation activities at its deep borehole demonstration centre in Texas. The company said the work marks an early milestone under an April 2026 federal agreement to help promising energy technologies move from the lab to commercial-scale pilot deployment. That agreement saw Deep Isolation selected for the US Department of Energy’s ARPA-E Scaleup Ready programme, which committed up to $40m (€35.9m) to support two projects, including the Deep Isolation project.

title: Deep Fission signs Kansas power agreement following market woes
summary: Last week, reactor developer Deep Fission announced that it had entered into a master energy purchase agreement with the Great Plains Development Authority in Kansas. This new milestone for the Department of Energy–backed start-up comes as it weathers the fallout from a recent report by a short-seller firm that accused the company of exaggerating its commercial viability.

title: Constellation to get up to $5B DOE loan for planned uprates
summary: Constellation has a conditional loan agreement of up to $5 billion in place with the Department of Energy’s Office of Energy Dominance Financing to support uprate projects at eight nuclear power plants in Illinois, Maryland, and Pennsylvania, the utility and federal agency announced Tuesday.

title: Entergy Mississippi responds to Lawrence County wildfire
summary: Entergy Mississippi has de-energized distribution lines that serve approximately 179 customers in Lawrence County near Monticello – due to the spreading wildfire in the area. The temporary power outage is expected to last until approximately 7 p.m., though the outage could be extended until conditions are safe. Source

title: Entergy Louisiana launches $2 million bill credit program for eligible customers
summary: Entergy Louisiana is launching a $2 million bill assistance program to help residential customers manage higher household costs. Beginning Oct. 28 at 9 a.m., eligible customers can apply for a one-time $100 bill credit issued through their local United Way. Source

title: European GenAI Platform Now Runs In Production Across All Swiss Nuclear Power Plants
summary: GRAYOAK Nuclear, a European provider of generative AI for the nuclear sector, has confirmed that its platform is now in active use at every Swiss nuclear power plant, developed in close partnership with operator Axpo. Twelve months after go-live, the system – known internally as “Lise” – processes more than 1,800 messages per day and has indexed over 550,000 documents spanning more than 50 years of operational history, with an 80% active-user rate among staff
